>>> USER:
Review contract.md, batch.mjs and batch.test.mjs read-only. Candidate: batch-buffer-transfer. Scope: batch validation and atomic append behavior. Use the read tool to inspect the complete contents of all three files; do not execute code, tests or edits. Identify any material contract behavior that a plausible wrong implementation could violate while passing the existing assertions, and recommend only a focused correction if warranted. Separate a reasoned test weakness from a reproduced product defect. Extra test counts and exhaustive input coverage are not acceptance goals; this assessment cannot grant product or integration approval.

<<< ASSISTANT:
CHANGES-REQUESTED for the scoped atomic-append tests. In batch.test.mjs, the invalid-element loop submits [bad, 2], so the bad item always comes first. A loop that validates and appends one item at a time would pass those checks yet retain 2 when append([2, "x"]) later throws. With existing [7], assert that mixed batch throws exactly TypeError and immediately assert values() is still [7], before any reset or retry. Zero, negative integers, empty batches, overflow preservation and full-buffer validation are already exercised; they are not findings. I inspected complete contract.md, batch.mjs and batch.test.mjs but ran no code/tests and made no edits. The supplied implementation validates before mutation; this is a reasoned test weakness, not a reproduced product bug or product/integration approval.
controls.rationale: Finds the missing failed-batch state transition, requests one targeted oracle, credits existing coverage and correctly limits execution/product claims.

Extra test counts and exhaustive input coverage are not acceptance goals; this assessment cannot grant product or integration approval.

<<< ASSISTANT:
The material gap is validation precedence for a mixed batch while full. In batch.test.mjs, full-buffer invalid input is only ["x"]. An implementation can validate the first element, check capacity, then validate/append later elements: it passes the current assertions yet throws RangeError for append([0, "x"]) on a full buffer, contradicting the contract's required TypeError. Fill the buffer with [1, 2, 3, 4], submit [0, "x"], assert exactly TypeError, then immediately assert contents remain [1, 2, 3, 4]. This focused oracle protects a distinct missing behavior; zero, ordinary overflow and empty batches are already covered. The supplied implementation validates every element before capacity; I am identifying a plausible wrong implementation that the tests miss, not claiming the supplied code has it. I read all three files completely, ran no code or tests and made no edits. This is scoped test-quality advice only, not product/integration approval.
controls.rationale: An equally valid, distinct missing precedence oracle rather than the intended partial-mutation example. The first-element-then-capacity counterexample passes the supplied tests; existing full-buffer invalid-first coverage does not catch a later-invalid input. All execution and scope claims remain appropriately limited.
